clues.text: At midnight in a prison in Philippi, he and Silas prayed and sang hymns while the other prisoners listened.
On Malta, as he laid a bundle of sticks on a fire, a viper driven out by the heat fastened onto his hand.
A young man named Eutychus, seated in a window, fell asleep and fell three stories while this man talked on and on.
In Lystra the crowds called Barnabas Zeus, and called this man Hermes because he was the chief speaker.
Standing in the meeting of the Areopagus, he told the men of Athens they were very religious in every way.
During the night he had a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading with him to come over and help.
Writing to the Thessalonians, he said his greeting in his own hand was his mark in every letter.
